text:
alex: Heads up — we have a sustained east-west latency spike from tor-7 affecting internal L4 LB traffic. Packet loss ~2-6% seen by backends since 08:12 UTC.
maya: :eyes: any obvious fanouts? which racks and LBs?
alex: Mainly rack tor-7 -> tor-8 path, but load balancer fanout shows many flows hairpinned through the local ToR instead of going to remote pool. GPU training burst kicked in and traffic patterns changed.
sam: Can you paste the LB health logs? also which backend instances?
alex: quick excerpt from lb-proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-18T08:12:19Z lb-proxy[pid=421]: backend 10.11.7.45 health=up/healthy RTT=12ms errors=0
2026-03-18T08:12:21Z lb-proxy[pid=421]: backend 10.11.7.52 health=degraded RTT=180ms errors=4
2026-03-18T08:12:35Z lb-proxy[pid=421]: route tor-7 -> local-backend queue=512 drop=14
```
not huge errors but sustained RTT spikes.
jordan: Got switch counters from tor-7: ifInDiscards=1248 ifOutDiscards=0 tx_pause=312 rx_pause=298 CRC=2. looks like ingress queue drops.
maya: That points at MTU or buffer mismatch or microbursts. Any RDMA traffic?
alex: Yes, training jobs do RDMA (GPUDirect) on the host side. But when flows hairpin through LB they get encapsulated and fall back to TCP. Suspect encapsulation + small buffers = amplification.
sam: Can you run `tc -s qdisc show dev <iface>` on an affected host and on the ToR uplink? Also capture some pcap to confirm re-transmits.
alex: Running now, attaching snippets: 
```
# host eth0
qdisc mq 0: dev eth0 root\n Sent 1.2G bytes  packet 1254434 errors 0\n backlog 0b requeues 0
qdisc fq_codel 0: dev eth0 parent 1:0\n Sent 1.2G bytes packet 1254434 drop 58 overlimits 0

# tor-7 uplink
qdisc pfifo_fast 0: dev Bond1 root\n Sent 12G bytes packet 11M errors 0\n backlog 0b requeues 0 drop 1200
```
seems host fq_codel dropping on encapsulated flows and ToR pfifo dropping upstream.
monitoring-bot: [alert] tor-7: egress queue drop rate > 1000/min since 08:14 UTC (severity=major).
jordan: If pfifo is the default on the switch ASIC, microburst from RDMA traffic could overflow buffers. Are jumbo frames enabled? MTU mismatch between host and switch could force fragmentation.
maya: We had a recent config change last week to disable jumbo on the LB VTEPs — could that be it? @sam do you remember?
sam: I pushed the change: VTEP MTU 1500 to match cross-dc overlay for stability. Hosts still set to 9000 for GPUDirect. That mismatch will fragment overlay packets and increase queue occupancy. :facepalm:
alex: So overlay encapsulated RDMA traffic (orig 9000) becomes several 1500 fragments -> lots more packets -> queue blowup. Explains amplification.
jordan: Quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily enable jumbo on VTEP and ToR uplinks (risky), 2) change LB to avoid hairpin and route to remote pool (software fallback), 3) throttle RDMA training jobs. Which do we want?
maya: For immediate relief, can we change LB policy to prefer non-local backends (avoid hairpin) and roll that for tor-7 only?
sam: I can flip a per-route policy to prefer cross-rack pool with weighted routing. Will do a canary on two nodes. Command: 
```
# on lb-control
lbctl routes update --route tor-7 --prefer remote_pool --canary 2
```
alex: Doing that now. Will monitor.
monitoring-bot: [info] route change applied (route=tor-7 prefer=remote_pool canary=2).
(4m later)
sam: Canary shows drop rate down 70% and backend RTT normalized. tor-7 egress drops falling.
jordan: Nice. Next steps: audit MTU across overlay, coordinate to either set jumbo end-to-end for RDMA lanes or force host-side overlay MTU to 1500 for encapsulated flows and use path MTU discovery. Also consider auto-avoid-hairpin policy for heavy RDMA flows.
maya: Also add an alert correlation between GPU scale-ups and tor egress drop rate so we can auto-trigger routing fallback.
alex: Filed follow-up ticket infra-ops#4321 for MTU remediation and routing policy change. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Created ticket infra-ops#4321: "tor-7 MTU + hairpin avoidance for RDMA-heavy workloads" assigned to sam, due 2026-03-25.
sam: I'll add a postmortem blurb after we verify jumbo plan in staging.
maya: Great, keep us posted.
